# Home

Welcome to my electronic portfolio!

I'm **Danny Halovanic**, a recent graduate from **West Chester University** with a B.S. in **Computer Science** and **Applied & Computational Mathematics**. I am passionate about information technology, technical support, and systems administration.

Currently, I serve as an **IT Intern at OTC Services**, where I provide Tier 1/2 technical support, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, manage user accounts in Active Directory, and assist with system deployments and network troubleshooting.

My academic background, combined with hands-on IT experience, has strengthened my problem-solving abilities and technical expertise across Windows, macOS, Linux, networking, and scripting environments.

This portfolio highlights my technical projects, professional experience, and the skills I have developed throughout my academic and professional journey.

# Projects

## Project 1: Comparing Methods for Finding Roots of Polynomials

This report explored and compared the performance of various root-finding techniques—both algebraic and numerical—for polynomials with extreme coefficient magnitudes. The focus was on assessing numerical stability, accuracy, and computational efficiency across methods such as the traditional algebraic formula, low-entropy expressions, as well as numerical methods such as Newton's and Bisection methods.

[View the report here (PDF)](assets/MAT_455_Report.pdf)

## Project 2: Modeling Prediction of Type II Diabetes in a Population
Using R Markdown and techniques from MAT 325 (Numerical Analysis I), this project modeled the prediction rate of Type II diabetes in the Pima Indian population. Statistical and numerical methods were employed to analyze trends, identify key predictors, and estimate the likelihood of diabetes occurrence based on various health indicators.

[View the project here (PDF)](assets/FinalProject.pdf)
